footer.ideaBody: There must be interesting analyses we haven't thought of! If you want to share an idea or have built something cool with the data, {email}
footer.dataBody: The full dataset is available to download - see {dataGuide} for links & info ({license}). Wondering about methodology, bias, or copyright? Read the {faq}.
footer.creditsBody: Open source: {github} and non-commercial. Only derived word counts are published - no subtitle text is redistributed.
footer.dataSourcesBody: Data: word counts from the {opus} (Lison & Tiedemann, 2016), via {openSubtitles}; film metadata from {imdbData} and {tmdb}. Information courtesy of IMDb ({imdbUrl}). Used with permission.
footer.tmdbDisclaimerBody: This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB. Posters via TMDB - copyright their respective studios, shown to identify the films discussed. Rights holder? {takedown} and it comes down promptly.
footer.madeByBody: Made by Andrew Beveridge - {github} · {linkedin} · {instagram} - with the original idea by my lovely wife {lindsay} - check out her portfolio!

languageFilter.hint: Filters by a film's original language; word counts come from the English subtitles.

filterExplainer.badgeTitle: Original language {lang} - counts come from the English translated subtitles. How does this work?
filterExplainer.filteringBody: {whatFiltering} a film's {originalLanguage} - where it was made, from TMDB metadata - not the language of the words below.
filterExplainer.wordsBody: {whatWords} every count on Movie Words comes from the film's {englishSubtitles}. We only have the English OpenSubtitles track, so for a non-English film these are the words of its {englishTranslation}, not the original dialogue. That's why an untranslated word occasionally slips through - "panna", "cotta", "samurai".
filterExplainer.spanishBody: {soSpanishMeans} the English-subtitle vocabulary of Spanish-{origin} cinema - how words like "solidarity" or "dictatorship" show up in the English subs of Spanish films - not Spanish words.
filterExplainer.dialogueNote: Original-language dialogue isn't in the dataset - just the English translation.
